title: Adaptive Quantum Security of Four-Round Luby–Rackoff
summary: The claimed adaptive quantum-CPA proof for four-round Luby–Rackoff is invalid, but a non-adaptive result is proved; a valid proof or the correct adaptive bound remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether $\operatorname{Adv}^{\mathrm{qcpa}}_{\mathrm{LR}_4}(A)=O\!\left(\sqrt{q^3/2^n}\right)$ admits a valid proof, or establish the correct adaptive bound.

scope.domain: Quantum security analysis of the four-round Luby–Rackoff Feistel construction.
assumptions: The adversary operates with adaptive quantum chosen-plaintext access.
parameters: A: adversary whose qCPA advantage is measured
q: query parameter in the claimed advantage bound
n: size parameter in the claimed advantage bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the claimed adaptive qCPA bound has a valid proof or establish the correct adaptive bound.

citations.label: Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs

progress.summary: The paper identifies a gap invalidating the claimed adaptive quantum-CPA proof, emphasizes that this is not an attack, and proves only a non-adaptive replacement. It notes that the issue persists even with arbitrarily many rounds.
citation_labels: Ritam Bhaumik et al., Mind the Bad Norms: Revisiting Compressed Oracle-based Quantum Indistinguishability Proofs
